title: Americans’ views of Israelis have grown increasingly negative, but views of Palestinians have held fairly steady
summary: Americans' views of the Israeli people and government have grown more negative across party lines and age groups, while opinions of Palestinians have held largely steady.

title: U.S. Hispanics Are Divided on Whether Their Identity Helps or Hurts Them in America
summary: Some say being Latino is a source of advantage or connection but others say it is tied to barriers and discrimination.

summary: Fifty years ago, Congress passed a law to improve data collection on people in the United States who have roots in Spanish-speaking countries – a group that came to be labeled “Hispanics” and “Latinos” in federal surveys and publications. title: Latino Trump voters are less likely than Harris voters to say being Latino is central to their lives
summary: Latino voters who supported President Donald Trump in 2024 differ from those who supported Democratic candidate Kamala Harris not only in their political views, but also in how central their Latino identity is to their lives. Across multiple measures, Trump voters are less likely to see their Latino background as central to who they are […]

title: Latino immigrants and U.S.-born Latinos differ on how much their identity shapes their lives
summary: For U.S. Latinos, the importance and meaning of identity are closely tied to how far they are from their family’s immigrant experience. summary: Over 100 countries have enacted energy policy changes in response to the Middle East conflict, from tax adjustments to fuel subsidies.

title: NATO Gets High Marks From Member States
summary: NATO is seen positively in most of 13 member states surveyed. Across 37 countries, views of Russia are negative and most people lack confidence in Putin and Zelenskyy.

title: How do right-wing populists view Russia, NATO and Zelenskyy?
summary: Europeans who support right-wing populist parties tend to have warmer views of Russia and Putin. Some feel especially favorably toward NATO, while others feel especially unfavorably.

title: Majority of Americans support banning social media for kids under 16
summary: Across major demographic and partisan groups, more Americans support than oppose banning those under 16 from using social media.

title: 5% of Americans say they’ve ridden in a driverless car
summary: Regardless of whether they’ve ridden in one before, most Americans (71%) say they would be not too or not at all comfortable riding in a driverless car.

title: About a third of U.S. Democrats like political leaders who identify as democratic socialists
summary: Democrats’ views on democratic socialists also differ by race and ethnicity, age, education, income and political engagement.

title: 5 facts about religion in the Philippines
summary: Nearly all Filipinos believe in God, most pray daily and 92% identify as Christian, with Catholics as the majority.

title: Which Americans are most likely to have spoken with a local journalist?
summary: About a quarter of Americans have spoken with a local journalist, with education, income, race and community attachment linked to higher rates of interaction.

title: Buying a home has gotten harder for young adults in most U.S. metro areas
summary: About nine-in-ten adults under 40 say buying a home is harder than it was for their parents, as rising prices and mortgage rates push homeownership further out of reach.

title: More than half of states restrict betting on elections
summary: Lawmakers in at least 16 states have introduced legislation this year to regulate prediction markets in some way.

title: What happens when war breaks out in the middle of a survey?
summary: Using statistical analysis of surveys fielded during the U.S.-Israel airstrikes on Iran, researchers tracked real-time shifts in global views of the U.S. and national economies.

title: Trump Gets Negative Reviews Internationally as Fewer Say U.S. Is a Reliable Partner
summary: A 36-country survey finds declining ratings for the U.S. amid rising concerns about its foreign policy and the health of its democracy.

title: How do views of Trump compare with other global leaders?
summary: Of the six leaders asked about, only Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu ranks below President Donald Trump in confidence.
